metadata.title: Campaign Momentum (Reinforcing Example)
metadata.description: A simple 3-node reinforcing loop used in the appendix to teach how to read a causal loop diagram. Strong polls attract donations, donations pay for ads, ads boost the polls — and the cycle accelerates.
metadata.author: US Government Intelligent Textbook

nodes.label: Poll Numbers
nodes.description: The candidate's current standing in public opinion polls.

nodes.label: Campaign Donations
nodes.description: Money flowing into the campaign from individual donors, PACs, and super PACs.

nodes.label: Ad Spending
nodes.description: Dollars spent on television, digital, and radio advertising to reach voters.

edges.description: Donors prefer to back winners. Higher poll numbers attract more donations.
More money in the bank means more dollars available to spend on advertising.
Advertising increases name recognition and persuades undecided voters.

loops.label: R1: Campaign Momentum
loops.description: A self-feeding cycle where every turn amplifies the candidate's lead. Sometimes called the 'bandwagon effect.'
loops.behavior_pattern: Exponential growth — until something outside the loop (a scandal, debate gaffe, primary loss) breaks it.
